# Commands

<!-- Generated by docs/generate.sh from `pub ... --help`; don't edit by hand. -->

```text
The curl for messaging

Usage: pub <COMMAND>

Commands:
  send     Send a message to a destination
  recv     Receive messages from a destination [alias: receive]
  browse   Show a queue's messages without consuming them
  unsub    Remove a durable subscription [alias: unsubscribe]
  move     Move messages to another destination on the same broker, transactionally
  dest     List, create and delete destinations [alias: destinations]
  ping     Connect, handshake and show server information
  alias    Manage host aliases (~/.pub/config.d)
  config   Inspect or initialise configuration
  modules  List protocol modules, their schemes and supported commands [alias: protocols]
  formats  List message formats (-F) and header strategies (--header-strategy)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Targets are URLs (amq://host:61616/queue/orders) or aliases from ~/.pub
(`pub alias add jms.company.com amq://mq01.company.com:61616`), optionally
followed by a path: jms.company.com/queue/orders

Configuration: ~/.pub/config and ~/.pub/config.d/* (git-config syntax);
set PUB_HOME to use another directory.
```

## pub send

```text
Send a message to a destination

Usage: pub send [OPTIONS] <TARGET>

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  URL (scheme://host[:port]/destination) or alias[/destination]

Options:
  -u, --user <USER[:PASS]>             Credentials as user[:password]
  -k, --insecure                       Skip TLS certificate verification
      --cacert <FILE>                  Extra CA certificates (PEM) to trust
      --tlsv1.2                        Accept TLS 1.2 or newer (default minimum is 1.3)
      --tlsv1.3                        Require TLS 1.3
      --tls-max <VERSION>              Highest TLS version to offer (1.2 or 1.3)
      --ciphers <LIST>                 Allowed TLS cipher suites, in preference order (comma or colon separated)
      --curves <LIST>                  TLS key exchange groups, in preference order, e.g. X25519:P-256
      --cert <FILE>                    Client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --key <FILE>                     Client private key (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --connect-timeout <DURATION>     TCP connect + TLS handshake timeout [default: 5s; 0 = none]
      --send-timeout <DURATION>        Timeout for a blocked socket write [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --receive-timeout <DURATION>     Timeout for an expected server reply, e.g. handshake or receipt [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --no-keepalive                   Disable TCP keepalive probes (on by default)
      --keepalive-time <DURATION>      Idle time before the first keepalive probe [default: 30s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-interval <DURATION>  Time between unanswered keepalive probes [default: 10s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-count <N>            Unanswered keepalive probes before the connection is dropped [default: 3; 0 = OS default]
      --receive-buffer <BYTES>         SO_RCVBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
      --send-buffer <BYTES>            SO_SNDBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
  -O, --option <KEY=VALUE>             Set a module/connection setting, e.g. -O vhost=prod -O receipts=false
  -v, --verbose...                     Show connection details and protocol frames on stderr (-vv: no truncation)
      --dest <DEST>                    Destination (overrides the URL path)
  -d, --data <DATA>                    Message body; @FILE reads a file, @- reads stdin
  -f, --file <FILE>                    Read the message body from FILE (- for stdin)
  -H, --header <NAME: VALUE>           Header: a standard field (priority, correlation-id, ttl, JMSType, ... see `pub config headers`), else a String property (repeatable)
  -P, --property <NAME[:TYPE]=VALUE>   Application property, optionally typed: -P orderId:long=42 (types: string, bool, byte, short, int, long, float, double) (repeatable)
  -t, --content-type <TYPE>            Content type header
  -n, --count <N>                      Send the message N times (with -F: every message in the input, N times) [default: 1]
  -F, --format <FORMAT>                Input format: raw (the input is the body; default) or a document format holding whole messages, e.g. json (see `pub formats`)
      --dest-from-input                Send each message to the destination its document names (falls back to the URL path / --dest)
      --header-strategy <STRATEGY>     How headers of messages read from a document are treated: default (new message-id and timestamp, original ttl from now) or administrative (admin; exact message-id, timestamp and expiration)
      --transaction                    Send everything in one local transaction: all or nothing
      --batch <N>                      With --transaction: commit every N messages
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## pub recv

```text
Receive messages from a destination

Usage: pub recv [OPTIONS] <TARGET>

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  URL (scheme://host[:port]/destination) or alias[/destination]

Options:
  -u, --user <USER[:PASS]>             Credentials as user[:password]
  -k, --insecure                       Skip TLS certificate verification
      --cacert <FILE>                  Extra CA certificates (PEM) to trust
      --tlsv1.2                        Accept TLS 1.2 or newer (default minimum is 1.3)
      --tlsv1.3                        Require TLS 1.3
      --tls-max <VERSION>              Highest TLS version to offer (1.2 or 1.3)
      --ciphers <LIST>                 Allowed TLS cipher suites, in preference order (comma or colon separated)
      --curves <LIST>                  TLS key exchange groups, in preference order, e.g. X25519:P-256
      --cert <FILE>                    Client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --key <FILE>                     Client private key (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --connect-timeout <DURATION>     TCP connect + TLS handshake timeout [default: 5s; 0 = none]
      --send-timeout <DURATION>        Timeout for a blocked socket write [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --receive-timeout <DURATION>     Timeout for an expected server reply, e.g. handshake or receipt [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --no-keepalive                   Disable TCP keepalive probes (on by default)
      --keepalive-time <DURATION>      Idle time before the first keepalive probe [default: 30s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-interval <DURATION>  Time between unanswered keepalive probes [default: 10s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-count <N>            Unanswered keepalive probes before the connection is dropped [default: 3; 0 = OS default]
      --receive-buffer <BYTES>         SO_RCVBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
      --send-buffer <BYTES>            SO_SNDBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
  -O, --option <KEY=VALUE>             Set a module/connection setting, e.g. -O vhost=prod -O receipts=false
  -v, --verbose...                     Show connection details and protocol frames on stderr (-vv: no truncation)
      --dest <DEST>                    Destination (overrides the URL path)
  -n, --count <N>                      Stop after N messages (0 = until --wait expires) [default: 1]
  -m, --wait <DURATION>                How long to wait for messages, e.g. 10, 10s, 2m [default: forever]
  -i, --include                        Print message headers before each body (same as -F text)
  -F, --format <FORMAT>                Output format: raw (bodies; default), text (as -i), json, ... (see `pub formats`)
  -o, --output <FILE>                  Append message bodies to FILE instead of stdout
  -l, --lines                          Ensure each body ends with a newline (default when stdout is a terminal)
  -s, --selector <EXPR>                Only receive messages matching this selector, e.g. "priority > 4 AND region = 'EU'"
      --selector-file <FILE>           Read the selector from FILE (also -sf; '-' = stdin; lines starting with # are comments)
  -H, --header <NAME: VALUE>           Raw protocol header for the subscription, passed through verbatim (repeatable)
      --no-ack                         Don't acknowledge messages (auto-ack mode)
      --durable <NAME>                 Receive through the durable topic subscription NAME (created if new; needs a fixed client-id); `pub unsub` removes it
      --transaction                    Acknowledge in a local transaction committed at the end; a failure (e.g. writing the output) rolls back and the messages stay on the broker
      --batch <N>                      With --transaction: commit every N messages
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## pub browse

```text
Show a queue's messages without consuming them

Usage: pub browse [OPTIONS] <TARGET>

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  URL (scheme://host[:port]/destination) or alias[/destination]

Options:
  -u, --user <USER[:PASS]>             Credentials as user[:password]
  -k, --insecure                       Skip TLS certificate verification
      --cacert <FILE>                  Extra CA certificates (PEM) to trust
      --tlsv1.2                        Accept TLS 1.2 or newer (default minimum is 1.3)
      --tlsv1.3                        Require TLS 1.3
      --tls-max <VERSION>              Highest TLS version to offer (1.2 or 1.3)
      --ciphers <LIST>                 Allowed TLS cipher suites, in preference order (comma or colon separated)
      --curves <LIST>                  TLS key exchange groups, in preference order, e.g. X25519:P-256
      --cert <FILE>                    Client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --key <FILE>                     Client private key (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --connect-timeout <DURATION>     TCP connect + TLS handshake timeout [default: 5s; 0 = none]
      --send-timeout <DURATION>        Timeout for a blocked socket write [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --receive-timeout <DURATION>     Timeout for an expected server reply, e.g. handshake or receipt [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --no-keepalive                   Disable TCP keepalive probes (on by default)
      --keepalive-time <DURATION>      Idle time before the first keepalive probe [default: 30s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-interval <DURATION>  Time between unanswered keepalive probes [default: 10s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-count <N>            Unanswered keepalive probes before the connection is dropped [default: 3; 0 = OS default]
      --receive-buffer <BYTES>         SO_RCVBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
      --send-buffer <BYTES>            SO_SNDBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
  -O, --option <KEY=VALUE>             Set a module/connection setting, e.g. -O vhost=prod -O receipts=false
  -v, --verbose...                     Show connection details and protocol frames on stderr (-vv: no truncation)
      --dest <DEST>                    Queue (overrides the URL path)
  -n, --count <N>                      Show at most N messages (0 = the whole queue) [default: 0]
  -m, --wait <DURATION>                Stop after this long, e.g. 10s [default: when the queue has been read]
  -i, --include                        Print message headers before each body (same as -F text)
  -F, --format <FORMAT>                Output format: raw (bodies; default), text (as -i), json, ... (see `pub formats`)
  -o, --output <FILE>                  Append message bodies to FILE instead of stdout
  -l, --lines                          Ensure each body ends with a newline (default when stdout is a terminal)
  -s, --selector <EXPR>                Only show messages matching this selector
      --selector-file <FILE>           Read the selector from FILE (also -sf)
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

```text
      --curves <LIST>                  TLS key exchange groups, in preference order, e.g. X25519:P-256
      --cert <FILE>                    Client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS

      --receive-timeout <DURATION>     Timeout for an expected server reply, e.g. handshake or receipt [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --no-keepalive                   Disable TCP keepalive probes (on by default)
      --keepalive-time <DURATION>      Idle time before the first keepalive probe [default: 30s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-interval <DURATION>  Time between unanswered keepalive probes [default: 10s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-count <N>            Unanswered keepalive probes before the connection is dropped [default: 3; 0 = OS default]
      --receive-buffer <BYTES>         SO_RCVBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
      --send-buffer <BYTES>            SO_SNDBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
  -O, --option <KEY=VALUE>             Set a module/connection setting, e.g. -O vhost=prod -O receipts=false
  -v, --verbose...                     Show connection details and protocol frames on stderr (-vv: no truncation)
      --durable <NAME>                 The durable subscription to remove (with the same client-id that created it)
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## pub move

```text
Move messages to another destination on the same broker, transactionally

Usage: pub move [OPTIONS] --to <DEST> <TARGET>

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  URL (scheme://host[:port]/destination) or alias[/destination]

Options:
  -u, --user <USER[:PASS]>             Credentials as user[:password]
  -k, --insecure                       Skip TLS certificate verification
      --cacert <FILE>                  Extra CA certificates (PEM) to trust
      --tlsv1.2                        Accept TLS 1.2 or newer (default minimum is 1.3)
      --tlsv1.3                        Require TLS 1.3
      --tls-max <VERSION>              Highest TLS version to offer (1.2 or 1.3)
      --ciphers <LIST>                 Allowed TLS cipher suites, in preference order (comma or colon separated)
      --curves <LIST>                  TLS key exchange groups, in preference order, e.g. X25519:P-256
      --cert <FILE>                    Client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --key <FILE>                     Client private key (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --connect-timeout <DURATION>     TCP connect + TLS handshake timeout [default: 5s; 0 = none]
      --send-timeout <DURATION>        Timeout for a blocked socket write [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --receive-timeout <DURATION>     Timeout for an expected server reply, e.g. handshake or receipt [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --no-keepalive                   Disable TCP keepalive probes (on by default)
      --keepalive-time <DURATION>      Idle time before the first keepalive probe [default: 30s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-interval <DURATION>  Time between unanswered keepalive probes [default: 10s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-count <N>            Unanswered keepalive probes before the connection is dropped [default: 3; 0 = OS default]
      --receive-buffer <BYTES>         SO_RCVBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
      --send-buffer <BYTES>            SO_SNDBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
  -O, --option <KEY=VALUE>             Set a module/connection setting, e.g. -O vhost=prod -O receipts=false
  -v, --verbose...                     Show connection details and protocol frames on stderr (-vv: no truncation)
      --dest <DEST>                    Source destination (overrides the URL path)
      --to <DEST>                      Target destination on the same broker, e.g. /queue/orders
  -n, --count <N>                      Move at most N messages (0 = until the source is quiet) [default: 0]
  -m, --wait <DURATION>                Stop when no message has arrived for this long [default: 1s]
      --batch <N>                      Commit every N messages (each batch moves completely or not at all) [default: 100]
  -s, --selector <EXPR>                Only move messages matching this selector
      --selector-file <FILE>           Read the selector from FILE (also -sf)
      --durable <NAME>                 Move from this durable subscription of the source topic
  -F, --format <FORMAT>                Also write each moved message, in this format (raw, text, json, ...)
  -o, --output <FILE>                  Write moved messages to FILE (with -F; default stdout)
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

## pub dest list

```text
List the broker's queues and topics, one per line (queue://NAME, topic://NAME)

Usage: pub dest list [OPTIONS] <TARGET>

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  URL (scheme://host[:port]/destination) or alias[/destination]

Options:
  -u, --user <USER[:PASS]>             Credentials as user[:password]
  -k, --insecure                       Skip TLS certificate verification
      --cacert <FILE>                  Extra CA certificates (PEM) to trust
      --tlsv1.2                        Accept TLS 1.2 or newer (default minimum is 1.3)
      --tlsv1.3                        Require TLS 1.3
      --tls-max <VERSION>              Highest TLS version to offer (1.2 or 1.3)
      --ciphers <LIST>                 Allowed TLS cipher suites, in preference order (comma or colon separated)
      --curves <LIST>                  TLS key exchange groups, in preference order, e.g. X25519:P-256
      --cert <FILE>                    Client certificate (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --key <FILE>                     Client private key (PEM) for mutual TLS
      --connect-timeout <DURATION>     TCP connect + TLS handshake timeout [default: 5s; 0 = none]
      --send-timeout <DURATION>        Timeout for a blocked socket write [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --receive-timeout <DURATION>     Timeout for an expected server reply, e.g. handshake or receipt [default: 10s; 0 = none]
      --no-keepalive                   Disable TCP keepalive probes (on by default)
      --keepalive-time <DURATION>      Idle time before the first keepalive probe [default: 30s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-interval <DURATION>  Time between unanswered keepalive probes [default: 10s; 0 = OS default]
      --keepalive-count <N>            Unanswered keepalive probes before the connection is dropped [default: 3; 0 = OS default]
      --receive-buffer <BYTES>         SO_RCVBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
      --send-buffer <BYTES>            SO_SNDBUF size, e.g. 256k, 4m [default: OS autotuning]
  -O, --option <KEY=VALUE>             Set a module/connection setting, e.g. -O vhost=prod -O receipts=false
  -v, --verbose...                     Show connection details and protocol frames on stderr (-vv: no truncation)
      --queues                         Only queues
      --topics                         Only topics
      --all                            Include the broker's own destinations (e.g. ActiveMQ.Advisory.*)
  -m, --wait <DURATION>                How long to listen for the broker's list (it has no end marker) [default: 1s]
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

```text
Usage: pub config path

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## pub config init

```text
Create ~/.pub with a commented starter config

Usage: pub config init

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## pub config check

```text
Validate all config files against the settings schema

Usage: pub config check

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## pub config settings

```text
List the settings pub understands (core, or one module's)

Usage: pub config settings [OPTIONS] [MODULE]

Arguments:
  [MODULE]  Module name, e.g. openwire; omit for all

Options:
      --markdown  Print Markdown tables (for the documentation)
  -h, --help      Print help
```

## pub config headers

```text
List standard message headers and how each module carries them

Usage: pub config headers [MODULE]

Arguments:
  [MODULE]  Module name, e.g. openwire; omit for all

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```
